projects.title: StockGenie
projects.description: Inventory and point-of-sale system for small businesses, combining stock control, checkout workflows, authentication, searchable data tables and PDF reporting.

caseStudyData.lead: A Laravel-based inventory and point-of-sale system that brings stock management, sales transactions, reporting and day-to-day administration into one responsive workflow.

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: Small businesses need a simple way to keep products, stock levels and sales transactions synchronized without the overhead of enterprise software.
StockGenie brings those core operations into a focused administrative workflow built for everyday use.

sections.title: How it was approached
paragraphs: The application centers the experience around inventory and checkout. Laravel handles application structure and authentication, while Bootstrap, DataTables and notification components support efficient administration.

cards.title: Inventory management
cards.description: Manage product details, categories and stock levels while maintaining inventory records.

cards.title: POS workflow
cards.description: Process sales through a checkout flow with inventory updates.

cards.title: Reporting
cards.description: Generate downloadable PDF reports for sales, inventory and business metrics.

cards.title: Data operations
cards.description: Use sortable and searchable DataTables to make administrative data easier to work with.

sections.title: Implementation stack
paragraphs: The implementation combines a Laravel backend with responsive administration components, searchable data tables and PDF reporting.

sections.title: What this project demonstrates
paragraphs: StockGenie demonstrates end-to-end Laravel application development across authentication, transaction-oriented workflows, reporting, data management and responsive business UI.
Future improvements can include broader automated testing, deployment automation and deeper usability evaluation.

projects.title: E-Commerce Platform
projects.description: Laravel e-commerce application with catalog management, authentication, order processing, inventory visibility, role-aware administration and manual payment workflows.

caseStudyData.lead: A Laravel commerce platform for small businesses that combines product administration, customer ordering, inventory visibility and controlled back-office workflows.

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: Running a small online store requires reliable catalog administration, inventory visibility and an order workflow that stays manageable for a small team.
The platform brings storefront activity and administrative control into a structured Laravel application.

sections.title: How it was approached
paragraphs: Customer ordering and administrative management are separated into clear workflows, with Laravel handling application logic, MySQL persistence and authentication/permission controls.

cards.title: Catalog management
cards.description: Add, edit, update and delete products, categories and subcategories.

cards.title: Inventory awareness
cards.description: Surface sales totals, current inventory levels and low-stock alerts.

cards.title: Order lifecycle
cards.description: Allow customers to place orders while administrators complete or cancel them.

cards.title: Access control
cards.description: Use Breeze authentication and Laratrust roles/permissions as the basis for protected workflows.

sections.title: Implementation stack
paragraphs: The implementation uses Laravel, MySQL and Bootstrap with authentication, permissions, searchable data tables and notification components.

sections.title: What this project demonstrates
paragraphs: The project demonstrates practical commerce architecture, CRUD-intensive administration and role-aware workflows for products, inventory and orders.
Future improvements can include online payment integration, automated testing and production deployment hardening.

projects.title: Hospital Management System
projects.description: Responsive multi-page healthcare interface exploring clear navigation, role-oriented information and structured presentation for hospital services and administration.

caseStudyData.lead: A multi-page hospital-management interface exploring navigation, doctor and administration views, and structured presentation of healthcare information.

sections.title: The problem
paragraphs: Healthcare interfaces bring together many roles, services and information types, making clear navigation and information hierarchy essential.
This project explores those needs through a structured multi-page interface.

sections.title: How it was approached
paragraphs: The interface separates administrative and doctor-oriented areas while maintaining consistent navigation and visual structure across pages.

cards.title: Information architecture
cards.description: Organize hospital content into understandable sections and navigation.

cards.title: Role-oriented pages
cards.description: Explore distinct admin and doctor-facing areas in the repository structure.

cards.title: Responsive presentation
cards.description: Present the public-facing experience in a browser-accessible format.

cards.title: Iterative learning
cards.description: Use the project as a foundation for learning how larger operational systems are structured.

sections.title: Implementation stack
paragraphs: The project uses front-end web technologies to organize a multi-page healthcare experience with responsive layouts and structured content.

sections.title: What this project demonstrates
paragraphs: This project represents an earlier stage of my web-development work and shows progression toward more complete full-stack business applications.
Future improvements can include a production backend, stronger accessibility, automated testing and more formal usability evaluation.
